svg.title: Heart failure decision chart: confirm with natriuretic peptide, ECG and echo, then sort the unstable patient by congestion (wet or dry) and perfusion (warm or cold) into acute treatment, and the stable patient by ejection fraction into reduced (diuretic, triple therapy, then ARNI, ivabradine, SGLT2 inhibitor and devices in order) or preserved (diuretics and risk factors)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Breathless, edematous, tired: is it HEART FAILURE (HF), and is the patient UNSTABLE now?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: a syndrome: typical symptoms + structural heart disease · the ejection fraction (EF) is not needed to diagnose it

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 1 · natriuretic peptide (BNP): LOW rules HF out → 2 · ECG: normal makes reduced EF very unlikely → 3 · ECHO, the gold

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: ACUTE decompensated: is it WET (congested)? is it COLD (hypoperfused)?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: WARM + DRY: adjust the oral therapy · look for the trigger: infection, anemia, thyroid, ischemia

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: CHRONIC: what is the EF on echo?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: New York Heart Association (NYHA) class: I no symptoms · II mild

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: III comfortable only at rest · IV symptoms at rest

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: every drug: start LOW, double every 2–4 weeks, check K+ and creatinine
